rationale: Ground truth is empty (bot rate-limit notice plus a bare 'lgtm'), so recall is vacuous for both. Both candidates independently converge on the same real findings — the residual pure-diffusion serving_tokenization=None path and the untested real-base() error path — which cross-validates those as genuine rather than fabricated. X is more actionable (ships a concrete helper-function fix and inline test code) but pads its review with many unverifiable external claims (upstream file/line citations, Docker pin details, a speculative sibling-rename sweep) and is internally inconsistent, labeling a residual issue 'blocking-ish' while still verdicting Approve. Y stays tighter to the diff, cites evidence lines for every claim, correctly identifies the diffusion-mode issue as pre-existing/nit rather than a regression, and its COMMENT verdict is better calibrated to what is otherwise a clean mechanical rename.
